claim: 150-300 minutes moderate or 75-150 minutes vigorous aerobic activity weekly
primary_case: Strong public-health recommendation with broad health and function benefits
adversarial_challenge: Benefits begin below the range; exact mix and upper dose are individual; decades-long mortality RCTs are unavailable
umbrella_action: Core range; emphasize that any activity is better than none

claim: Strengthen all major muscle groups across at least 2 days weekly
primary_case: Strong guideline support for strength; function; bone and metabolic health
adversarial_challenge: No universal exercise; set; load; or session duration is established
umbrella_action: Core; use progressive tolerable training across major muscle groups

claim: Move more and sit less
primary_case: Guidelines support replacing sedentary time with activity and count bouts of any length
adversarial_challenge: No validated universal sitting limit or mandatory hourly break interval
umbrella_action: Core principle without a timer-based prescription

claim: At least 7 hours of sleep with reasonably regular timing
primary_case: Consensus supports at least 7 hours; timing regularity is associated with health and performance
adversarial_challenge: Individual sleep need varies; timing-outcome evidence is largely observational; more than 9 hours can be appropriate during recovery
umbrella_action: Core duration; regularity is a moderate-evidence support rather than a minute-level rule

claim: Morning outdoor light and lower evening light
primary_case: Light timing affects circadian phase and is associated with sleep timing
adversarial_challenge: Healthy-adult studies are heterogeneous and often observational; clinical outcomes and a universal duration are unproven
umbrella_action: Optional sleep-schedule experiment; not a core anti-aging practice

claim: Varied minimally processed nutrient-dense diet
primary_case: Convergent dietary guidance supports variety; plants; whole grains; pulses; nuts and unsaturated fats
adversarial_challenge: Minimally processed is imprecise; long-term pattern evidence includes residual confounding; cultural flexibility matters
umbrella_action: Core food pattern without dietary purity rules
key_sources: WHO Healthy Diet 2026; 2025-2030 US Dietary Guidelines

claim: At least 400 g vegetables and fruit and 25 g naturally occurring fiber daily
primary_case: WHO strong population recommendations
adversarial_challenge: Not magic thresholds; abrupt fiber increases can cause symptoms; individual energy and GI needs differ
umbrella_action: Core practical target with gradual progression

claim: Protein floor 0.8 g/kg/day and 1.2-1.6 g/kg/day for resistance-training muscle goals
primary_case: RDA supports adequacy; resistance-training meta-analysis shows small added gains and plateau around 1.6 g/kg/day
adversarial_challenge: The upper range is not a universal longevity target and requires contextualization for medical conditions and body size
umbrella_action: Core adequacy; conditional training range

claim: Hydrate to thirst and conditions without a universal gallon target
primary_case: National Academies indicates thirst and ordinary drinking generally maintain hydration in healthy people
adversarial_challenge: Thirst can be unreliable in some older adults and medical settings; forced drinking during endurance activity can cause hyponatremia
umbrella_action: Core support; individualize for heat; exertion; illness; pregnancy or clinician restrictions

claim: Avoid tobacco and recreational nicotine
primary_case: Tobacco has broad causal harm and nicotine is addictive
adversarial_challenge: Approved nicotine replacement can be appropriate for cessation and should not be confused with recreational use
umbrella_action: Core harm reduction; prioritize evidence-based cessation support

claim: Minimize alcohol; not drinking is lowest exposure
primary_case: Alcohol causes dose-related cancer; injury and organ risk; no need to start for health
adversarial_challenge: Risk magnitude varies by dose and pattern; most population harm is concentrated in heavier and episodic use
umbrella_action: Core: less is better; zero is valid; avoid moralized wording

claim: Broad-spectrum SPF 30+ on exposed skin
primary_case: Randomized evidence supports reduced photoaging; authoritative guidance supports sunscreen plus clothing and shade
adversarial_challenge: The photoaging trial was one population; indoor-only daily use and a specific product are not established; 24% was relative odds not wrinkle count
umbrella_action: Core during meaningful UV exposure; pair with clothing and shade

claim: Fluoride toothpaste twice daily for about two minutes
primary_case: Strong caries-prevention evidence and ADA guidance
adversarial_challenge: Technique; fluoride concentration and personal caries risk matter; premium toothpaste is not inherently superior
umbrella_action: Universal oral-care core

claim: Daily interdental cleaning
primary_case: ADA recommends daily cleaning and short trials support plaque or gingival outcomes
adversarial_challenge: Cochrane certainty is low or very low; long-term caries and periodontitis outcomes and device superiority are unproven
umbrella_action: Core care standard; allow floss; interdental brush or water flosser fitted to anatomy

claim: Basic cleanser; moisturizer; hair; body; nail and foot care
primary_case: Low-burden practices support comfort; cleanliness; barrier care and cosmetic maintenance
adversarial_challenge: No broad longevity outcome; over-washing; fragrance and aggressive grooming can cause harm
umbrella_action: Support only; do not frame grooming as systemic anti-aging

claim: Meaningful social connection
primary_case: Large prospective associations and public-health advisories link isolation with worse health
adversarial_challenge: Much evidence is observational; social interventions vary; no universal contact frequency or lifespan effect is established
umbrella_action: Core life domain without a numeric dose
key_sources: US Surgeon General Social Connection Advisory

claim: Meaningful cognitively challenging activity
primary_case: Some cognitive interventions produce small improvements in cognitive tests
adversarial_challenge: WHO rates cognitive training evidence low and cognitive stimulation evidence very low; neither has demonstrated a dementia-incidence benefit or a validated dose
umbrella_action: Optional for function and enjoyment; not a health quota or dementia-prevention prescription
key_sources: WHO Dementia Risk-Reduction Guideline Second Edition

claim: Repeatable stress-management practice
primary_case: Trials and reviews show modest improvements in perceived stress; anxiety and related outcomes
adversarial_challenge: Heterogeneous; often short-term; not mandatory; adverse experiences occur; no anti-aging or telomere guarantee
umbrella_action: Offer methods only when they measurably help

claim: Vaccinations and evidence-based risk-specific screening
primary_case: Strong preventive guidance with meaningful disease outcomes
adversarial_challenge: Schedules depend on age; anatomy; pregnancy; occupation; geography and risk; blanket tests cause harm
umbrella_action: Core preventive plan; source schedules dynamically from CDC and USPSTF

claim: Adult blood-pressure screening with confirmation after an elevated office result
primary_case: USPSTF Grade A for adults; treatment of confirmed hypertension improves hard outcomes
adversarial_challenge: No trial directly randomizes screening versus no screening; optimal interval varies; home checking after a normal screen can add noise
umbrella_action: Explicit core preventive item without mandatory home monitoring

claim: Sexual and reproductive prevention matched to goals and exposures
primary_case: Contraception or pregnancy planning; barriers and HIV/STI testing can prevent important outcomes when applicable
adversarial_challenge: Needs vary by anatomy; practices; partners; symptoms; pregnancy; location and goals; a universal cadence would overgeneralize
umbrella_action: Include as risk- and goal-based preventive care rather than a daily task
key_sources: CDC STI Testing; CDC STI Prevention

claim: Abnormal screening findings require confirmation and evidence-based follow-through
primary_case: Screening only improves outcomes when a valid pathway confirms and addresses actionable risk
adversarial_challenge: Repeated self-testing can amplify noise and does not substitute for diagnosis or treatment
umbrella_action: State the follow-through rule explicitly; use the pathway appropriate to the finding

claim: Safety and environmental basics
primary_case: Seat belts; appropriate helmets; smoke and CO alarms and hearing protection prevent meaningful injury or exposure
adversarial_challenge: They are context-dependent safeguards rather than a daily wellness stack
umbrella_action: Always-on harm-reduction rules; not ritualized products

claim: Test every home for radon if status is unknown
primary_case: Radon is a causal lung-cancer hazard and testing is the only way to know a home's level
adversarial_challenge: Testing is occasional and only useful if elevated results lead to mitigation; risk and action thresholds vary by level and jurisdiction
umbrella_action: Compact home-safety action; once if unknown and after major occupancy or structural changes

claim: Wildfire-smoke and PM2.5 exposure plan
primary_case: Reducing indoor particles during smoke episodes is biologically and operationally credible; EPA supports source control and mechanical filtration
adversarial_challenge: Benefit depends on actual exposure; building leakage; device sizing and operation; routine purifier ownership is not universal
umbrella_action: Exposure-triggered plan; compatible MERV 13 or correctly sized HEPA; avoid ionizers and ozone

claim: Clean; separate; cook; and chill food
primary_case: Established food-safety guidance targets common contamination and temperature pathways
adversarial_challenge: Exact handling rules and risk differ by food and population; compulsive sanitation is unnecessary
umbrella_action: Compact everyday food-handling baseline

claim: Caffeine at the lowest effective dose; 400 mg/day ceiling for most healthy adults
primary_case: FDA population safety ceiling and trials support alertness and some performance effects
adversarial_challenge: Sensitivity and metabolism vary; 400 mg can disrupt sleep even many hours before bed; pregnancy; anxiety; arrhythmia and medications matter
umbrella_action: Optional; lowest dose; default early cutoff; ceiling is not a target

claim: Creatine monohydrate 3-5 g/day with resistance training
primary_case: Numerous trials support repeated high-intensity performance; strength and training adaptation
adversarial_challenge: Not a general health requirement; lean-mass change includes water; a direct-imaging meta-analysis found a very small and uncertain hypertrophy effect and reported industry-related conflicts; serum creatinine can mislead
umbrella_action: Goal-specific performance module; do not promise a specific muscle-gain amount

claim: Protein powder
primary_case: Equivalent protein can make intake convenient
adversarial_challenge: No intrinsic advantage over food; contaminants; allergens; calories and displacement of varied food matter
umbrella_action: Not a required supplement; prefer independent testing

claim: Prescription tretinoin for facial photodamage
primary_case: Controlled trials support improvement in facial photodamage signs
adversarial_challenge: Prescription cosmetic treatment; irritation and adherence burden; no systemic health or longevity benefit
umbrella_action: Optional advanced appearance care outside the universal core

claim: Routine multivitamin; omega-3; vitamin D or mineral stack without a demonstrated need
primary_case: Some agents help deficiencies; dietary restrictions or indicated populations
adversarial_challenge: No universal primary-prevention benefit; excess dosing and interactions are possible
umbrella_action: Use only for a dietary gap; life stage; deficiency or clinician-directed indication

claim: Routine CGM; microbiome; genetic; biological-age and broad biomarker testing in healthy adults
primary_case: Can produce data and may have research or condition-specific uses
adversarial_challenge: No validated general outcome pathway; false positives; anxiety; privacy and unnecessary restriction can outweigh value
umbrella_action: Exclude from core; test only when the result changes an evidence-based decision

claim: Cold plunge; sauna; red light; PEMF or hyperbaric oxygen as universal routine
primary_case: Some modalities have narrow indications; observational associations or short-term surrogate effects
adversarial_challenge: Heterogeneous small studies; modality-specific risks; no universal broad-health protocol or outcome advantage over the core
umbrella_action: May be leisure or condition-specific care; not routine human optimization

claim: Hormones; peptides; nootropics or condition-treatment drugs without an indication
primary_case: Some treatments are effective for diagnosed conditions
adversarial_challenge: Unapproved products; adverse effects; interactions; product-quality problems and absent general-health outcomes
umbrella_action: Diagnose and treat the condition; do not preemptively medicalize the healthy baseline
